fixes.explanation: Water, baker. The verse says it plainly: “They camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for the people to drink.” (Exodus 17:1) A whole nation pulls into camp, everybody drops their bags, and the first thing they hear is that there's nothing to drink. That's a one star review and a very short sentence.

That's the one, baker. The LORD says, “Take along in your hand the staff with which you struck the Nile, and go.” (Exodus 17:5) Moses already knows this staff, so he doesn't have to go shopping for a new one. Then the LORD says He will stand there before him by the rock at Horeb. (Exodus 17:6) I once kept my own tools close at hand too, because you never know which one the day is going to call for.

Strikes, baker! The LORD says, “And when you strike the rock, water will come out of it for the people to drink.” (Exodus 17:6) Think about that. A rock. In a desert. And the LORD says water is coming out of it. I've pressed a lot of dough in my day, and not once has a rock given me a drink. The LORD also says He will stand there before Moses by the rock, so Moses isn't doing this alone.

Joshua, friend! Moses tells him, “Choose some of our men and go out to fight the Amalekites.” (Exodus 17:9) Then the very next verse says Joshua did as Moses had instructed him. (Exodus 17:10) No arguing, no "let me think about it," no ten minute pause. I wish I'd been that quick the day I had to get out of bed and face a full batch of dough.
